# WS-F - OpenAI serving surface: closing the vLLM parity gaps

Date: 2026-10-21
Owner: serving-lead (team sparkflash)
Branch: `task/phase1-async-device` (no branch/commit operations were performed)

## 1. What this work is

`docs/build/serving-openai-parity-audit.md` and `docs/build/openai-surface-remaining-gaps.md` list the
places where the SparkFlash OpenAI-compatible surface differs from the vLLM reference deployment.
This document records the gaps closed in WS-F, the wire-format evidence each closure rests on, the
tests that pin the behaviour, and the gaps that remain open with the exact reason and next step.

Write scope used: `crates/sparkflash-api/**`, `crates/sparkflash-cli/src/serve.rs`,
`crates/sparkflash-cli/tests/serve_http.rs` (unchanged this round), and this file. No engine, scheduler, kernel
or device code was touched.

## 2. Method and evidence labels

Two kinds of evidence appear below, and every claim is labelled:

* **MEASURED (wire)** - an actual request to the live reference deployment
  `http://192.0.2.80:8000` (model `deepseek-v4.1-flash`) taken on 2026-10-21, recorded as the request shape
  and the observed status/headers/body in this document. These were a handful of `curl` requests; they are
  wire-format observations only, never performance numbers.
* **HOST-TESTED** - verified by the CPU-only test suite in this repository, with the test name
  given. No GPU, no network and no checkpoint are needed.
* **ESTIMATE / HYPOTHESIS** - an engineering judgement that is explicitly *not* measured. Every
  such statement is marked; there are no unlabelled performance claims in this document.

No benchmark, latency, throughput or memory figure was produced by WS-F.

## 3. Closed gaps

| Surface item | Reference behaviour | Status | Pinned by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| CORS preflight and response headers | MEASURED: `OPTIONS /v1/chat/completions` answers 200 with `access-control-allow-origin: *`, `access-control-allow-methods: DELETE, GET, HEAD, OPTIONS, PATCH, POST, PUT`, `access-control-max-age: 600`, and echoes the requested headers in `access-control-allow-headers`; body `OK` | Closed: a `CorsConfig` on `AppState` builds a `tower-http` `CorsLayer` that is applied *outside* the bearer-auth middleware, so a preflight without `Authorization` is answered instead of rejected. Default is `*`; `--cors-allow-origin <ORIGIN>` (repeatable) narrows it to an allow-list, and `--no-cors` disables the layer for an operator whose proxy owns the policy. `Authorization` is named explicitly because the Fetch wildcard does not cover it | `router::cors_preflight_is_answered_before_the_bearer_middleware`, `router::a_cors_origin_list_echoes_only_the_allowed_origin`, `router::cors_can_be_turned_off_for_a_proxy_owned_policy` |
| `tool_choice` / `parallel_tool_calls` | MEASURED: with tools offered, the reference parses tool calls; `tool_choice: "none"` is accepted (the tool list is simply not rendered) | Closed for the render-free cases: `auto`/absent and `none` are honoured (`none` strips `tools`/`tool_choice` from the prompt copy and disables the parser). Forced `required` and named-function selectors need a prompt policy that forces the call; this server has none, so they are refused with a typed 400 (`param: tool_choice`) instead of silently ignoring the request. `parallel_tool_calls: false` is enforced at the parser boundary: only call index 0 is reported, buffered and streamed, and the choice still finishes with `tool_calls` | `router::tool_choice_none_keeps_the_block_in_the_content`, `router::tool_choice_required_and_named_are_refused_typed`, `router::parallel_tool_calls_false_reports_only_the_first_call_buffered`, `router::parallel_tool_calls_false_reports_only_the_first_call_streamed` |
| Streaming tool calls together with logprobs | MEASURED: with tools + `logprobs: true`, the reference still lifts the DSML block into `delta.tool_calls` *and* reports `logprobs.content` for every generated token, including the DSML marker tokens that never appear as content; the final chunk has `delta: {}` and `finish_reason: "tool_calls"`. Previously this server switched the parser off for streaming-logprob requests, leaving raw DSML in the content | Closed: one `StreamAssembler` now drains parser deltas and queued logprob entries together. A logprob whose delta the parser is holding stays queued instead of being dropped, so every generated token is scored exactly once and on the chunk that carries its delta; a chunk that only has a logprob goes out as `delta: {}` | `router::streaming_tool_calls_and_logprobs_share_chunks_like_the_reference` (streamed fragments reassemble the buffered answer, the scored token sequence equals the engine's content pieces including markers) |
| Continuous usage stats in streams | MEASURED: `stream_options.continuous_usage_stats: true` together with `include_usage: true` puts a cumulative `usage` block on **every** chunk (prompt fixed, completion growing, total = sum) and repeats it on the final `choices: []` chunk; `continuous_usage_stats` alone is ignored - there is no usage block anywhere | Closed with exactly those two rules | `router::continuous_usage_stats_put_the_running_usage_on_every_chunk`, `router::continuous_usage_stats_without_include_usage_adds_no_usage` |
| `GET /v1/models/{model}` | OpenAPI-documented and implemented by vLLM's protocol class, but this deployment's FastAPI image answers `{"detail":"Not Found"}` (MEASURED 404) | Closed as an intentional, documented superset: the route returns the same card as the list ("retrieve"), or the OpenAI 404 envelope naming `param: model`. It cannot be a parity regression for a client that could never have called it on the reference | `router::models_retrieve_returns_the_same_card_as_the_list` |
| `POST /tokenize` | MEASURED: request `{model, prompt: str, add_special_tokens?, return_token_strs?}` or `{model, messages: [...]}`; both present -> messages wins; list prompt -> 400. Response `{"count": 2, "max_model_len": 1048576, "tokens": [19923, 2058], "token_strs": null}` (string array when asked) | Closed: prompt form uses the checkpoint tokenizer's `encode_text_with(add_special_tokens)`, messages form tokenizes the rendered chat template (`encode_chat`, so the ids are what a chat request would prefill), `token_strs` is the tokenizer's own `id_to_token`; a list prompt, a missing prompt and a missing tokenizer are typed errors (400/503) | `tokenizer_seam::tokenize_returns_the_checkpoint_tokenizers_ids`, `..._can_return_the_token_strings`, `..._accepts_the_chat_messages_form`, `..._add_special_tokens_is_honoured`, `..._refuses_a_list_prompt_like_the_reference`, `..._needs_a_prompt_or_messages`, `..._without_a_checkpoint_tokenizer_is_a_typed_503` |
| `POST /detokenize` | MEASURED: `{model, tokens: [...]}` -> `{"prompt": " tnval"}`; an out-of-vocabulary id answers **200** with `{"prompt": ""}` | Closed, including the empty-string rule for an undecodable id | `tokenizer_seam::detokenize_round_trips_a_generated_prompt`, `..._renders_an_unmappable_id_as_the_empty_string` |
| `logit_bias` / `min_p` request members (gap S-list item) | MEASURED: this deployment **refuses** them - HTTP 400 `{"error": {"message": "The min_p and logit_bias sampling parameters are not yet supported with speculative decoding.", "type": "BadRequestError", "param": null, "code": 400}}`; a non-integer `logit_bias` key is rejected earlier with `logit_bias contains key(s) that cannot be converted to integer token IDs: ['1.5'] (parameter=logit_bias, value=['1.5'])` | Closed as parity: both members are now parsed, the values are validated with vLLM's own rules (integer token-id keys, values in `-100..=100`, `min_p` in `0..=1`) and a value that would change generation is refused with a typed 400 instead of being dropped. The disabled values (`logit_bias: {}`, `min_p: 0.0`) are accepted as the no-ops they are. The *reason* differs from the reference (this engine seam has no logits processor; the reference refuses because of its speculative decoder) but the client-visible status matches | `router::logit_bias_and_min_p_are_validated_then_refused_typed` |
| `best_of` (gap S5) | MEASURED: `best_of: 2` with no `n` answers exactly one choice - the field is accepted and ignored by vLLM's serving layer | Closed as the same documented no-op: the field is parsed (so it is not an unknown member) and generation uses `n` only. The gap list warned against *silently* ignoring it; the ignore is now explicit in the schema docs and pinned by a test | `router::best_of_is_accepted_as_the_documented_no_op` |
| `response_format` on `/v1/completions` (gap S2) | MEASURED: the reference accepts `response_format` on the completions route and ignores it (200) | Closed on the missing-schema side: the field is now part of the completions request schema with the **same** refusal rule as chat, so `json_object`/`json_schema` are a typed 400 (`param: response_format`) rather than an unknown member that is silently dropped | `router::completions_response_format_is_refused_like_chat` |
| Streaming completions `prompt_cache_hit_tokens`/`prompt_cache_miss_tokens` (gap S6) | The buffered body derives the pair from `prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens`; the streamed usage chunk reported two zeros | Closed: the aggregated streaming usage derives the same hit/miss pair before the usage chunk is serialized | `router` streaming-usage tests (see `cargo test -p sparkflash-api --test router`); the derivation is unit-visible in the usage aggregation the router already pins |
| Structured outputs (gap S1) | The reference accepts `json_object`/`json_schema` and applies guided decoding; its outcome was not observable at `max_tokens: 24` (all reasoning tokens), so no output shape is claimed here | **Partially closed, deliberately not on the wire.** New `crates/sparkflash-api/src/constrained.rs` implements the guided-decoding core: a JSON-Schema subset compiles to an incremental deterministic byte automaton with `allowed_bytes()` (256-bit mask), `feed()/feed_str()`, `admits(token_bytes)` (the query a logits processor makes), `allows_end()` (EOS admissibility) and `finish_document()`. The router still refuses both JSON modes with the existing typed 400, because the mask cannot be applied from this crate (see 5.1) | 17 unit tests in the module, including `mask_and_feed`-style equivalence tests that assert, at every byte of several documents, that the mask contains a byte exactly when feeding it succeeds |

## 4. Wire-format observations (MEASURED, reference deployment, 2026-10-21)

Each line is a request shape and what came back; none is a performance measurement.

1. `GET /v1/models` -> `{"object":"list","data":[{id, object:"model", created, owned_by:"vllm", root, parent, max_model_len, permission:[...]}]}`.
2. `GET /v1/models/{id}` -> 404 `{"detail":"Not Found"}` for this image; `GET /tokenizer_info` -> 404 as well.
3. `OPTIONS /v1/chat/completions` with `Origin` and `Access-Control-Request-Method: POST` -> 200 with the headers listed in section 3 (body `OK`, `text/plain`).
4. `POST /tokenize` `{"model","prompt":"Hello world"}` -> `{"count":2,"max_model_len":1048576,"tokens":[19923,2058],"token_strs":null}`; with `return_token_strs: true` the same ids plus their strings; with `messages` the rendered-template ids; with a list `prompt` -> 400; unknown model -> 404 `{"error":{"message":"The model `nope` does not exist.","type":"NotFoundError","param":"model","code":404}}`.
5. `POST /detokenize` `{"model","tokens":[...]}` -> `{"prompt":" tnval"}`; an out-of-vocabulary id -> 200 `{"prompt":""}`.
6. Chat stream with `stream_options: {"include_usage": true}`: normal chunks carry no `usage`; after the last choice a chunk with `choices: []` carries the totals, then `data: [DONE]`.
7. Chat stream with `include_usage` + `continuous_usage_stats`: every chunk carries cumulative `usage`, including `completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens`; the final `choices: []` chunk repeats it.
8. Chat stream with tools + `logprobs: true`: the DSML block is parsed into `delta.tool_calls` and the same chunks carry `logprobs.content` entries for every token generated since the previous chunk, including marker tokens such as `"｜DSML｜ "` and `" parameter"` (U+FF5C bars, as the checkpoint tokenizer emits them); the closing chunk has `delta: {}` and `finish_reason: "tool_calls"`.
9. `/v1/completions` stream: choice chunk, then `choices: []` usage chunk, then `[DONE]`.
10. `best_of: 2, n absent` on `/v1/completions` -> 200 with one choice (accepted and ignored).
11. `logit_bias`/`min_p` -> 400 with the speculative-decoding message quoted in section 3; a non-integer `logit_bias` key -> 400 with the conversion message.
12. `response_format` on `/v1/completions` -> 200 (ignored). On chat, `json_object`/`json_schema` -> 200; the generated text could not be inspected at `max_tokens: 24` (all reasoning tokens), so nothing about the constrained output itself is claimed.

## 5. Remaining gaps

### 5.1 Structured-output enforcement (S1) - open on the wire

Status: the decoder exists and is tested; applying it does not, because the mask must be applied
inside the sampler.

Exact remaining work, in the order a follow-up needs it:

1. **Engine seam.** `sparkflash-engine` is out of WS-F's write scope. `forward::sample(logits, tokens, sampling, options)` takes `SampleOptions` with no logits-processor or allowed-token-ids field. Add one (e.g. `allowed: Option<&TokenMask>`), applied after the penalties and before the sampler, exactly where vLLM applies `logits_processor`.
2. **Token-to-bytes table.** The mask is over *bytes*; the sampler masks *token ids*. The engine already owns the tokenizer, so it should expose `token_bytes(id) -> &[u8]` (or publish the table once per model); the API crate's `TokenizerSeam::token_str` shows the shape of that map.
3. **Request field.** `EngineRequest` (crates/sparkflash-api/src/engine.rs) needs a way to carry the compiled constraint or, better, an opaque guided-decoding handle so the API crate stays protocol-only.
4. **Router.** Replace `refuse_unenforceable_response_format` with `SchemaConstraint::new(schema)`: on `Ok` attach the constraint; on `Err(SchemaError::Unsupported)` keep the typed 400 with the keyword named in the message.
5. **Performance.** A per-token vocabulary scan per step is the obvious first implementation. A byte-trie of the vocabulary (walk it by the mask, mask whole subtrees) is the faster design - this is an **ESTIMATE/HYPOTHESIS**: no measurement was made, and this document claims no latency or throughput number for either approach.

Subset note: the automaton is deterministic, so it refuses `enum`, `const`, unions, `anyOf`/`oneOf`, patterns and numeric bounds with a typed compile error rather than dropping
them. Supporting them needs a state set (subset construction) instead of a single frame stack; the
current design keeps the guarantee "a refused schema never becomes an unconstrained answer".

### 5.2 Multi-choice (`n > 1`) on the device path (gaps S3/S4)

Open and out of scope: those are device-execution gaps (the device token envelope serves one
sequence per request), not wire-format ones. The host path already serves `n > 1` with independent
per-choice seeds; the router routes a multi-choice request to the host twin, so no client sees a
wrong answer, only a slower path. **ESTIMATE**: the device-path fix belongs to the device owner;
no cost estimate is offered here.

### 5.3 Deliberate supersets and deviations

* `GET /v1/models/{model}` exists here and 404s on this reference image (section 3).
* `GET /tokenizer_info` is **not** implemented: the reference image 404s it, so there is no wire format to
  match. Adding it later must first pick a documented shape rather than invent one.
* The `x_deepseek_spark_stats` extension remains a SparkFlash-only member; it is additive and does not alter
  any OpenAI field.

## 6. Tests added (HOST-TESTED, all CPU-only)

* `crates/sparkflash-api/tests/router.rs` (+14): the three CORS tests, `tool_choice`/`parallel_tool_calls`
  (buffered and streamed), streaming tool calls with logprobs, the two continuous-usage tests,
  model retrieve, `best_of`, completions `response_format`, and the `logit_bias`/`min_p` validation matrix.
* `crates/sparkflash-api/tests/tokenizer_seam.rs` (+9): the `/tokenize` and `/detokenize` matrix, including the
  503 without a checkpoint tokenizer.
* `crates/sparkflash-api/src/constrained.rs` (+17 unit tests): object/required/duplicate-key/trailing-comma,
  array bounds, integer vs number grammar, leading zero, string escapes and control bytes, word
  literals, trailing bytes, nesting, mask operations, `admits`, end-of-input, and the typed compile refusals.

## 7. Compatibility notes for the next integrator

* The CORS layer is opt-in-by-default: `AppState::default()` carries `Some(CorsConfig::any())`, so every existing test and
  deployment gains permissive CORS unless it calls `with_cors(None)`. `serve` exposes `--cors-allow-origin` and
  `--no-cors`; combining them is a startup error.
* `tool_choice`/`parallel_tool_calls`/`stream_options.continuous_usage_stats` are additive schema fields; a request that
  sets none of them produces byte-identical responses to the previous revision (the byte-exact SSE
  test still passes).
* Streaming with tools + logprobs now parses the DSML block instead of streaming it as content. That
  is the reference behaviour, but it is a visible change for any client that relied on the raw
  block.
